calls.head: A shadow job for Foerster, Zegras and Konecny
calls.body: At home, the Flyers keep sending Konecny’s line (Foerster, Zegras and Konecny) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Tocchet has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Benson, Krebs and Thompson.
calls.call: The Flyers’ L2 (Foerster, Zegras and Konecny) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sabres’ first line, against about 36% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 55% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 36% with no line matching

chips.tip: Philadelphia’s L2 (Foerster, Zegras and Konecny) at home: 55% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Philadelphia home games this season, 11 games, 35 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 36% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Philadelphia’s L2 (Foerster, Zegras, Konecny) spent 21% of its 5-on-5 time against Buffalo’s L1 (2:21 of 11:13). The call needed 46%, halfway from the 36% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 55%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Foerster, Zegras and Konecny barely saw the Sabres’ first line
calls.plain: Philadelphia sent Foerster, Zegras and Konecny out against the Sabres’ first line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Tocchet sent them out against Kulich, Norris and Doan (3:38 of 11:13 at 5-on-5).
calls.said: Rick Tocchet would send Foerster, Zegras and Konecny out against the Sabres’ first line again

calls.head: Active D vs. forward-led
calls.body: The Sabres’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Flyers’ not so much. Buffalo is one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Philadelphia is one of the worst. Watch the Sabres’ defensemen jump into the play.
calls.call: The Sabres’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Flyers’.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Dvorak’s third-period goal lifts the Flyers past the Sabres
paras: Mattias Samuelsson got the scoring started for the Sabres just 47 seconds into the game, but Jamie Drysdale tied it up for Philadelphia early in the second. Tage Thompson put the Sabres back ahead 2-1 less than five minutes later. Owen Tippett made it 2-2 for Philadelphia three and a half minutes later, and Travis Sanheim put the Flyers ahead 3-2 just 29 seconds into the third. Jiří Kulich made it 3-3 for Buffalo just over four minutes later, with Thompson picking up his 200th NHL assist on the goal. Christian Dvorak put the Flyers ahead for good 52 seconds later.

The Flyers outshot the Sabres 33-19, but the Sabres’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. The Sabres hit two posts and the crossbar and came up a goal short. Joseph Woll made 16 saves for the Flyers, and Alex Lyon stopped 29 of 33 at the other end. The Flyers improved to 7-11-6, sixth in the Metropolitan, while the Sabres dropped to 8-9-4, sixth in the Atlantic.
